notes: There is no public transport in Phuket. Use a scooter (licence and helmet required), Grab or a hotel taxi. Tuk-tuks are expensive, so haggle.
November to April is dry with calm seas, so Phi Phi and Similan tours run reliably. December and January are the busiest months.
Book boat tours online with hotel pickup included. Bring seasickness tablets and reef-safe sunscreen.
Choose your seafood by the kilo at Rawai market; the cooking fee is charged separately per person.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples. On Bangla Road, ask the drink price first.
Skip elephant rides and choose ethical sanctuaries instead.

stops.name: Phuket Old Town Thalang Road
stops.tips: Colourful Sino-Portuguese shophouses. Cafes open in the morning, and on Sundays the street turns into a walking market.

stops.name: Phuket Thai Hua Museum
stops.tips: The history of Chinese migrants, in an air-conditioned old school building.

stops.name: One Chun Cafe Phuket
stops.tips: Michelin Bib Gourmand local cooking. Try the moo hong (braised pork belly) and the crab.

stops.name: Big Buddha Phuket
stops.tips: A 45 m marble Buddha on the hilltop with 360° views of the island. Cover shoulders and knees; get there by taxi or scooter.

stops.name: Wat Chalong
stops.tips: Phuket's most important temple, known for its tradition of making wishes with fireworks.

backups.name: Khao Rang Hill
backups.tips: A hilltop with city views, close to Big Buddha. A good alternative.

stops.name: Kata Noi Beach
stops.tips: A small, calm cove. Sunbeds cost 100 THB, and in the dry season you can snorkel.

stops.name: Kata Beach Street Stalls
stops.tips: Pad thai and mango sticky rice just behind the beach.

stops.name: Karon Beach
stops.tips: 3 km of sand. The wind picks up in the afternoon; good for a long walk.

stops.name: Karon Viewpoint
stops.tips: A lookout that takes in three bays at once. Go before sunset.

stops.name: Kata Night Market
stops.tips: A night market in central Kata with grilled seafood and roti.

backups.name: Kampong Kata Hill Restaurant
backups.tips: A Thai restaurant full of antiques, in Kata.

backups.name: Dino Park Mini Golf
backups.tips: A rainy-day option for families with kids, in Karon.

stops.name: Maya Bay
stops.tips: Speedboat tour (~1,800 THB, lunch included, hotel pickup at 08:00). Visits to Maya Bay are limited; you also stop at Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave.

stops.name: Pileh Lagoon
stops.tips: An emerald lagoon for snorkelling.

stops.name: Phi Phi Don Tonsai Village
stops.tips: Lunch in the island village (included in the tour) and a stroll through the shops.

stops.name: Bamboo Island
stops.tips: White sand and a last swim. The return leaves at 17:00.

stops.name: Rawai Seafood Market
stops.tips: Pick your fish at the market in Rawai and have it cooked across the way. Phuket's most famous seafood evening.

backups.name: Kan Eang at Pier Chalong
backups.tips: Seafood at Chalong Pier, as an alternative to Rawai.

backups.name: Coral Island Koh Hae
backups.tips: A nearby island for a half-day trip if Phi Phi is cancelled.

stops.name: Freedom Beach
stops.tips: An unspoilt cove reached by long-tail boat from Patong (~200 THB per person). The water is clear in the dry season.

stops.name: Patong Beach
stops.tips: The island's busiest beach. Good for walking and jet skiing (haggle).

stops.name: No.6 Restaurant Patong
stops.tips: A cheap Thai eatery in Patong. The queue moves fast; order the tom yum.

stops.name: Jungceylon Shopping Mall
stops.tips: An air-conditioned mall, handy for a break from rain or heat.

stops.name: Bangla Road
stops.tips: Patong's nightlife street, with bars and shows. Watch your wallet.

backups.name: Baan Rim Pa Patong
backups.tips: Royal Thai cuisine on the cliffs. Come for the sunset.

backups.name: Simon Cabaret Phuket
backups.tips: A cabaret show, as an alternative to Bangla Road.

stops.name: Nai Harn Beach
stops.tips: The island's best-loved quiet beach, with a lagoon and pine shade.

stops.name: Nai Harn Beach Stalls
stops.tips: Grilled food and fruit shakes just behind the beach.

stops.name: Windmill Viewpoint
stops.tips: A viewpoint by the wind turbine, looking over Nai Harn and Ya Nui.

stops.name: Promthep Cape
stops.tips: The island's southernmost tip and Phuket's most famous sunset. Arrive an hour early to get a spot.

backups.name: Rawai Beach Restaurant
backups.tips: Thai food on the Rawai seafront.

backups.name: Ya Nui Beach
backups.tips: A tiny snorkelling cove below Promthep.

stops.name: Similan Islands
stops.tips: Open from November to May. Thailand's best islands for snorkelling and diving, reached by speedboat (~3,500 THB), with hotel pickup at 06:00.

stops.name: Similan Boat Lunch
stops.tips: Lunch is included in the tour.

stops.name: Sailing Rock Koh Miang
stops.tips: The Similans' signature rock, with views from the top.

stops.name: Old Town Soi Romanee
stops.tips: The most photogenic street, best in the morning light.

stops.name: Torry's Ice Cream Phuket
stops.tips: Local ice cream in Old Town. Go for coconut.

stops.name: Blue Elephant Phuket
stops.tips: Royal Thai cuisine in a mansion. A fitting farewell lunch, and cooking classes are available too.

stops.name: Phuket Airport Road Sirinat
stops.tips: The airport is 45 minutes away. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Ka Jok See Phuket
backups.tips: Thai food in an old house.

backups.name: Sirinat National Park Nai Yang
backups.tips: A beach next to the airport, where you can watch planes land.
